verdict.rationale: Fly.io's own docs say it builds Machines from images users provide and converts Docker images into fast-booting VMs. `fly launch` can use a project's existing Dockerfile or generate one, then deploy the app. One community user reported that pushing simple containers failed 70-80% of the time, which lowers confidence in reliability but does not contradict the capability itself. Missing for 10: documentation on deploying prebuilt images from a registry, and independent hands-on corroboration that container deploys work reliably.

support.subject: As a developer, I can deploy applications packaged as Docker containers

citations.quote: Fly.io converts Docker images to fast-booting VMs and runs them globally.
We build Machines out of the images you give us and we run them where you tell us to.
If your project already has one, Fly Launch can use it instead.
Run `fly launch` from inside your project source directory to create, configure, and (for most apps) deploy a new application.
